global_attention_fixed_t3.finding: Only four blocks execute for T3; simple one-head block splitting duplicates K/V staging and is not an end-to-end win.

grouped_moe_gate_up.finding: The host upper bound launched 129 expert-tile rows for 24 assignments although every non-empty tile consumes at least one assignment.

t3_fused_gate_up_projection.finding: The unstaged short-batch kernel has only 1.1 blocks per SM; two warps per block doubles independent blocks without duplicating activation staging.

accepted_changes.description: Cap grouped expert launch rows by assignment_count, a strict upper bound on non-empty expert tiles.
Use two warps per block for unstaged fused Gate/Up projections with T<=3.

rejected_changes.description: Split fixed-T3 global attention from four query heads per block to one.
rejected_changes.reason: Fourfold K/V staging offsets the additional block parallelism.

rejected_changes.description: Use one warp per block for unstaged fused Gate/Up projections with T<=3.
rejected_changes.reason: Additional block scheduling and reduced per-block work regress versus the two-warp variant.

limitations: Each candidate is one warm-up plus three retained runs, not the final formal three-warm-up/ten-retained qualification.
Nsight Compute kernel replay makes the instrumented process exit after capture; reports are complete and only hardware counters, not profiled application throughput, are used.
The raw .ncu-rep files remain outside version control under /tmp.
The protected real 12B product test requires GEM16_12B_MODEL and was unavailable in this environment.
